title: Arsenal sign Martin Ødegaard and Aaron Ramsdale but will not stop there
trail: Martin Ødegaard has joined Arsenal in a permanent transfer from Real Madrid but will not be available to face Chelsea on Sunday
body: Mikel Arteta said Arsenal are not finished in the transfer market after completing a £34m deal for Martin Ødegaard and a £30m swoop for the Sheffield United goalkeeper Aaron Ramsdale, who signed on Friday afternoon. The manager remains keen to add further to his squad before the end of the month. Ødegaard spent the second half of last season on loan from Real Madrid, whom he joined aged 16, but has now signed on a permanent basis. He became Arsenal’s fourth major summer recruit following the arrivals of Ben White, Nuno Tavares and Albert Sambi Lokonga. He was swiftly followed by Ramsdale who completed his switch from Sheffield to Arsenal in a deal which is worth £24m up front with £6m in add-ons. Ødegaard will not be available for Sunday’s game against Chelsea as the club are awaiting visa clearance, Arsenal have confirmed. Arteta said the Norway midfielder “made us better” last season and provides creativity but the Arsenal manager is hopeful of further bolstering his squad. “There are still 11 days to go and we still have things to do,” Arteta said. “There are going to be players at the moment, the way the squad is set up that it is going to be difficult to find game time [for]. There are things to be done.” The Gunners host Chelsea on Sunday hoping to return to winning ways after an opening-day defeat to promoted Brentford. Arteta was without four players for that game – Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Alexandre Lacazette, Willian and Alex Rúnarsson – after the quartet returned positive Covid tests and the Arsenal manager said he was surprised the game was not postponed. “Yes, I was surprised [it was not called off]. But the regulators decided that the best thing to do was to play the game.” Arteta said he has urged his players to get vaccinated but recognises it is a delicate subject. “Most of them are double vaccinated,” he said. “Others have one vaccine. We are trying to encourage them to get vaccinated because they are going to protect themselves, their families and the environment around the club, but it is a really personal matter. We are trying to guide them and explain the reasons why it is better to do it but at the end it is a personal decision.” Arsenal’s poor performance against Brentford led to widespread criticism but Arteta insisted he will not listen to outside noise. “I want people that are constructive around me,” said the Spaniard. “I know the people who have intentions to bury us, to try to criticise us. We are not interested in that. We have a lot of positives, a lot of new energy that is coming up. My full focus is on that and finding a way to beat Chelsea.” Arteta steered clear of naming names but said some people have been “very disrespectful” towards his team and acknowledged it is “nothing new”. The former Arsenal striker and now pundit Paul Merson called the club’s recruitment under technical director Edu “lazy”, while Paul Kagame, the president of Rwanda – whose government sponsor the club – was critical of the team’s performance in defeat at Brentford. “We just must not excuse or accept mediocrity,” Kagame tweeted. “I agree that Arsenal should not accept mediocrity,” said Arteta. “I totally agree.”
